claim: The least weakly prime-additive positive integer of length \(4\) is \(8610\). More precisely, \(\kappa_n\ne4\) for every \(n<8610\), while \(\kappa_{8610}=4\), and its unique four-term representation up to ordering the summands is \[8610=3^8+5^2+7^3+41^2.\] Here \(\kappa_n\) is the minimum number of distinct prime divisors \(p_i\mid n\) whose positive powers sum to \(n\).
integrity: The proof of minimality is an exhaustive exact-integer enumeration over all positive prime powers attached to distinct prime divisors for every integer through 8610.
The computation is supplied as a standalone standard-library checker and was replayed from the packaged file.
The database occurrence of 8610 is treated as prior evidence and not as proof of its exact length or minimality.
scientific_limitations: This is an exact finite least-element theorem, not an infinitude or density result.
It does not classify all weakly prime-additive integers of length 4 beyond the least example.
Originality remains subject to the residual possibility of an unindexed computation not found in the inspected sources.
title: The least length-four weakly prime-additive number is 8610
